newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to ensure citizen access in privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to ensure citizen access in privatisations.

text.p: Taiwan's top economic planning body said on Monday it would release shares of large state-run companies to citizens through preferential treatment to prevent concentrated buying by conglomerates.

"We have commissioned a research group to propose the preferential treatments to encourage all nationals to buy shares of large state-run firms," an official at the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development told Reuters.
The plan was to follow the example of Singapore Telecommunications Ltd's successful privatisation, he said.
Details of how the state would ensure citizen access have yet to be completed but would be announced in January, he said.
Since 1989, the government has raised T$145.2 billion by selling off state shares, he said.

In previous privatisations, local media and market analysts cried foul after private conglomerates moved in to take control of some state firms as they were sold off, saying the government should reform its procedures to ensure broad ownership by Taiwan citizens of equity once owned by the state.
